title: Adaptive comm sparsity + pipeline stall autopsy
content:
Summary:
This is a working autopsy of a recurring tail-latency issue observed on multi-GPU inference rigs running pipeline+tensor parallel blends. Symptoms: intermittent ~3-10x spikes in end-to-end request latency (p95->p99.9), correlated with NVLink utilization microbursts and repeated pipeline stage stalls. Unlike previous NCCL bandwidth saturation tickets, these events appear to be caused by transient large AllGather/Reduce sizes combined with aligned tensor chunk boundaries across ranks, creating synchronized host-to-device queuing and tiny window packet storms on NVLink.

Hypothesis:
1) Static chunking used by the runtime aligns chunk boundaries across all pipeline stages which amplifies periodic full-KV cache transfers and large AllGather sizes at predictable intervals.
2) These aligned transfers overwhelm per-link buffering, producing microburst backpressure which stalls DMA and kernel launch paths, increasing queuing on host->device and causing p99 spikes.
3) NCCL's algorithm choice at those message sizes (allgather recursive vs ring) interacts poorly with topology (mixed nvlink+pcie) and results in uneven per-link load.

Why this doc exists:
- We previously focused on bulk bandwidth averages; this investigation targets sub-ms burstiness and scheduling alignment.
- Goal: produce changes we can A/B (dynamic chunk off-alignment and comm-sparsity with selective zero-skipping) and measure p99 improvement without reducing throughput.

Testbed and workloads:
- 8x A100-sxm4 (NVLink fully connected in bisection topology similar to prod-dedicated-64g nodes)
- Runtime build: feature/elastic-chunking branch (bench harness included)
- Models: Llama-2-13B in 4-way tensor-parallel, 2-way pipeline-parallel (total 8 ranks per micro-batch)
- Input distribution: mix of short/long prompts (seq=64 and seq=1024) weighted 70/30 to emulate product mix
- Measurement hooks: kernel timestamps (CUDA events), nvlink counters via nvidia-smi dmon + NVLink error counters, nsight systems capture for 10s windows, NCCL_TRACE=INFO logs

Baseline run (static-chunking):
- Aggregate tokens/sec: 3200
- mean latency: 22ms, p95: 42ms, p99: 180ms, p99.9: 820ms
- Observed microburst signature: repeated 200-300us NVLink saturations every 12ms aligned to model KV flushes.
- NCCL collectives around bursts: AllGather sizes ~40MB, repeated across 8 ranks. NCCL chose recursive doubling for some sizes on this topology.

Experiment 1: Staggered chunk offsets (random seed per-rank offset)
- Change: offset tensor chunk boundaries by 1/num_chunks * (rank_index) (deterministic stagger), so not all ranks perform big transfers simultaneously.
- Result: tokens/sec -2.5% (3180); mean latency ~+1ms; p95 improved to 35ms; p99 improved to 120ms; p99.9 improved to 340ms.
- Observation: NVLink microbursts still occur but with much lower peak amplitude and decorrelated timing across ranks. Backpressure events reduced by ~60% in nsight timelines.

Experiment 2: Topology-aware NCCL algorithm hinting + small-slab aggregation
- Change: force NCCL to use ring for mid-size collectives and aggregate small slabs into ~16MB transfers instead of 40MB to increase packet interleaving.
- Result: tokens/sec +1% over baseline; p99 dropped to 95ms; p99.9 dropped to 260ms.
- Observation: ring better balanced link usage on this node-level topology; however larger message count increased CPU/NIC interrupt overhead slightly.

Experiment 3: Adaptive comm-sparsity (drop zeros in AllGather KV slices)
- Change: runtime inspects KV slice sparsity and sends compressed bitmap+dense only for non-empty rows (lossless); falls back when compression ratio <1.1.
- Result: tokens/sec +3%; mean latency -1.8ms; p95 30ms; p99 80ms; p99.9 200ms.
- Observation: For real-inference traffic with long context windows where prefix keys are often padded zeros or deterministic masks, compression reduced transfer sizes and eliminated several microbursts. CPU encoding overhead visible but acceptable under our CPUs.
- Caveat: not applicable to quantized models where zero patterns differ. Need detection heuristics per model.

Experiment 4: Combined strategy (stagger + topology NCCL hint + adaptive sparsity)
- Result: tokens/sec +2.8%; p99 45ms; p99.9 120ms. Stable under 8-hour soak with mixed workload.

Micro-level observations (from nsight timeline captures):
- When bursts occurred, the sequence was: host enqueues big DMA -> NVLink link level buffer fills -> kernel launches queue up waiting on input tensors -> compute stalls and out-of-order completion -> NCCL re-tries small control msgs -> additional host-side queuing.
- Host->device PCIe DMA seemed unaffected; path-level congestion concentrated on NVLink bisection links between certain pairs of GPUs.
- Some outlier traces show GPU-side tail stalls due to small (~64KB) page fragmentations creating extra PCIe descriptors; mitigations may require page-aligned pinned buffers.

Practical recommendations (short-term):
1) Implement deterministic staggered chunk offsets by default (config flag: runtime.chunk_stagger=rank_stride). Low risk, no model changes.
2) Add topology-aware NCCL hinting for mid-sized collectives; maintain a small matrix of heuristic thresholds per instance type.
3) Enable adaptive comm-sparsity as opt-in per model; provide a dry-run mode that only logs potential savings (no compression) to avoid regressions.
4) Add NVLink microburst counters into trace pipeline (nsight-style capture sampling) and expose a simple "burstiness index" in Console per node.

Longer-term work (backlog):
- Explore packet pacing inside the runtime to smooth NVLink bursts without reducing aggregate throughput (centisecond-level pacing).
- Investigate kernel placement strategies to avoid aligning large KV transfers with peak generate token windows (temporal reshuffling).
- Evaluate hardware-level mitigations: page-aligned pinned buffers by default, NVLink QoS if available, or small hardware prefetch throttling where supported.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How does quantization (4-bit fused kernels) change sparsity patterns? Initial microbench suggests less zero-skipping benefit; need dedicated runs.
- Can we generalize bitmap compression format for GPU-side decompression to remove CPU overhead? Prototype PR #893 has a GPU decompress path but needs perf sign-off.
- Should stagger be deterministic (rank-based) or dynamic (based on observed recent microbursts)? Dynamic may adapt better but is more complex.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Ava: land deterministic-stagger patch + e2e test (ETA 1 week)
- Ravi: prototype topology-NCCL hinting in infra images (ETA 2 weeks)
- Lena: run compression dry-run across top-10 models and report model-wise win-rate (ETA 2 weeks)
- Tomás: add NVLink burstiness metric to trace pipeline and dashboard mockup (ETA 3 weeks)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc records iteration notes; expect follow-up PRs and an internal RFC once we confirm stability in Dedicated clusters.
- If you are triaging prod tail spikes and have captured nsight traces or NCCL logs, attach them to JIRA-ENG-1427 and ping here.

Appendix (commands & snippets):
- nvprof / nsight capture snippets: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nvlink --output=trace.nsys python -m serving.bench --model llama-2-13b --tp 4 --pp 2 --duration 60
- quick NCCL logging: export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO && export NCCL_TOPO_FILE=/etc/nccl/topo.xml && ./run_inference_bench.sh |& tee nccl.log
- quick-check bitmap compression ratio: python tools/kv_sparsity_estimator.py --capture sample-kv.npy --threshold 0.02

End of notes.
